newsitem.title: HUNGARY: MOODY UPGRADE FIRMS HUNGARY ON DEBT MARKETS - C.BANK.
newsitem.headline: MOODY UPGRADE FIRMS HUNGARY ON DEBT MARKETS - C.BANK.

text.p: The upgrade of Hungary's debt by Moody's Investors Service on Friday may further improve the country's position on debt markets, but Hungary does not plan to take up new loans, National Bank of Hungary President Gyorgy Suranyi told Reuters on Friday.

"This is our sixth investment grade (from international rating agencies) this year," Suranyi said. "This is a further good signal, which confirms what the past few months' processes showed and what was already felt much earlier.

Moody's upgraded the sovereign ceiling for foreign currency debt of Hungary to Baa3 from Ba1 on Thursday, for foreign currency bank deposits to Ba1 from Ba2 and the short-term sovereign ceiling for foreign currency notes and bills to Prime-3 from Not Prime.

Suranyi said the interest rate conditions for new loans which Hungary would take up could further improve due to the move of Moody's, but this also depended on the future liquidity of international markets.
Hungary said earlier that it was not likely to need loans from abroad in 1997 and it would only tap the international markets if it could further improve the interest conditions of its loans.
Suranyi said Hungary did not have any plans to borrow from abroad but did not rule out that it would take up loans in 1997.
"Currently we do not plan to enter the market," he said. "We announced in November that we would repay $1 billion before maturity and we are carrying out that programme."
